sections.overview: The dwarf spotted wobbegong is a small carpet shark endemic to southwestern Western Australia.
sections.identification: It reaches up to 94 cm total length; its colourful, spotted appearance once led to confusion with the larger spotted wobbegong, O. maculatus.
sections.habitat: It is a bottom-dweller of inshore waters and the continental shelf, recorded at depths of 9–135 m.
sections.diet: Its species-specific diet remains poorly documented in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: It lives on the seabed; no distinct activity schedule is established in the sources used here.
sections.reproduction: The consulted assessment provides no species-specific reproductive measurements.
sections.ecology: Described with O. floridus in 2008, it is sympatric with that smaller-range cousin; the two are separated by a combination of colour and anatomical traits.
sections.conservation: The 2025 global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern and reports a stable population trend.

sources.title: Two new wobbegong sharks, Orectolobus floridus and O. parvimaculatus — Zootaxa
